newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Futures can help Australian woolgrowers - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Futures can help Australian woolgrowers - ABARE.

text.p: Australian woolgrowers could significantly reduce their price risk by using futures contracts, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.

Analysis revealed that about 17 percent of Australia's woolgrowers could reduce their price risk by 90 percent by hedging their wool through futures contracts, ABARE said while releasing a research report.

About 45 percent could reduce their price risk by at least 80 percent and nearly 30 percent could probably cover less than 50 percent of their price risk, Brian Fisher, ABARE's executive director, said in a statement.
Growers no longer had the floor price which had operated in varying forms between 1971 and 1991 and which had reduced the need to hedge against price downturns, he said.
The report contains results of quantitative analysis of the type and quantity of wool that might be hedged effectively using futures contracts.
Fibre diameter largely determined the level of risk reduction that could be realised, Fisher said.
The effectiveness of a hedge declined at an increasing rate the further the fibre diameter deviated from the Sydney Futures Exchange's contract specification of 21 microns, he said.
For wools over 24 microns the hedge became speculative, he said.
Management of risk reduction was widely acknowledged as a significant problem facing many Australian wool growers, he said.
